Race name: Widdy's Work presents Stomp Out the Stigma
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
STOMP OUT THE STIGMA is all about raising awareness of mental wellness and eliminating the stigma surrounding mental illness. Join us in the fastest, flat 5k route in the area or a nice 1 mile race around Waughop Lake. Parking will be easy at the Pierce College Fort Steilacoom campus with a short walk down a trail to Fort Steilacoom Park. The 5k race starts by the lake where you will fly through a flat course at Fort Steilacoom Park and finish back at the entrance of the lake. The 1mile race starts at the entrance of Waughop Lake and takes you on a scenic lap around the lake. Both routes are mostly paved with a short area that is dirt/gravel. This 5k race is chip timed. The entry includes a race shirt if you register by 7/21. Finishing medals will be given to the first 200 finishers. Don't miss the chance to be a part of this great event! Sorry… no strollers or dogs at the event because of the insurance restrictions.

Whether you walk for yourself, for someone you love, or simply to make a difference, we invite you to be part of this meaningful CoastBusters Walk and the community it brings together.

Description:
Join us June 6, 2026 and get ready to Conquer the Canyon - HALF MARATHON (13.1 miles), 10K, and 5K! And the return of the 5K Doggie Dash! Cruise through Redmond’s Dry Canyon Trail which boasts stunning high desert geological features and peaceful scenic surroundings. The majority of the Dry Canyon is a nature preserve with steep rocky walls - a tribute to the area’s volcanic past. The course also weaves through Redmond's town center. Catch impressive natural views and traditional city scenes featuring pavilions and historic landmarks. Choose your distance: 5K, 10K or 1/2 marathon. RACE SCHEDULE Packet Pickup: Friday, June 5 from 2-6pm at SCP Redmond Hotel (Downtown Redmond). You may also pick up your packet one hour before your race time at the race. RACE START TIMES Half Marathon - 9am 10K - 9:15am 5K - 9:30am 5K Doggie Dash - 9:33am Starting line and finish and after party is in Centennial Park in Redmond. All finishers receive a custom-made medal, food and drink at the after-party!

Race name: 2026 Salmon Run
Listed distance: 13.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Join us for the 38th annual Salmon Run which returns to Bend, Oregon on April 18, 2026. Distances include the HALF MARATHON (13.1 miles), 10K, and 5K races. All courses weave along the beautiful Deschutes River on trails and some pavement. Taking place in the spring, the Salmon Run is one of the first running events of the season and the essential tip-off to the local racing scene in Central Oregon. Traversing beautiful dirt and paved trails amongst junipers and pines, the race course winds through some of the most scenic natural areas in Bend and finishes on the lawn Riverbend Park. Make a weekend of it! Course Details The Salmon Run course takes runners along the beautiful and picturesque Deschutes River. The half marathon course is 75% paved sidewalks and 25% trail. The 10K course is 80% paved sidewalks and 20% trail. The 5K is 65% paved sidewalks and 35% trail. All courses will be marked with a combination of mile markers and directional arrows. Finish Line Festivities Enjoy a post-race party with delicious food and beverages (beer!) and music. We’ve got gift bags and awards for the top three male and female finishers in both open and master’s categories! 1st, 2nd & 3rd place ribbons for top age-group finishers. Parking for Race Day There is limited parking at Riverbend Park on race day. We highly recommend carpooling. Parking attendants will direct you as you arrive. Additional parking is available on City streets. For full details regarding the Salmon Run, click here.

After his passing, his loved ones created a scholarship in his memory and established an annual pickleball tournament to fund it. St. Mary's Academy is proud to support this tournament as a tribute to the Garrett Family. Jeanne, Steve's wife, was a valued employee of the school for many years, and both of them were active volunteers at various events as parents and members of the community. The pickleball tournament has become a beloved annual event, bringing together players of all skill levels and ages. It's a day filled with friendly competition, laughter, and community spirit. Participants come from all over the region to take part in the tournament and support the scholarship fund. Listed distance: 1.5 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Ovarian Cancer About 21,010 women in the United States are expected to be diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2026 — that’s roughly one diagnosis every 25 minutes. In Oregon and Washington, the American Cancer Society estimates 1,610 new diagnoses. These are our grandmothers, mothers, sisters, partners, colleagues, and friends. Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecologic cancer and the fifth leading cause of cancer-related death among women in the United States. Because symptoms are often subtle and easily dismissed, nearly three-quarters of cases are diagnosed after the cancer has spread beyond the ovaries. While the overall five-year survival rate is about 50 percent, survival drops significantly — to around 30 percent — when the disease is diagnosed at a distant stage. Call to Action: Teal Ribbon Fun Walk These statistics make one thing clear: awareness matters. That’s why OCAOSW is hosting the 4th Annual Teal Ribbon Fun Walk on June 27, 2026. There is currently no reliable screening test for ovarian cancer, which makes education about symptoms and risk factors critical. When ovarian cancer is detected at an earlier stage, survival rates improve significantly — and informed communities are better equipped to act. This 1.5-mile walk at the Oregon Zoo brings together survivors, families, friends, and advocates in visible support of those impacted by ovarian cancer. Race name: Best in the West Triathlon Festival
Listed distance: 70.3 Miles
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Best in the West Triathlon Festival - Designed by athletes, for athletes! Nestled in the foothills of the Cascades and fed by the Santiam River, Foster Reservoir offers premier recreation facilities to the outdoor enthusiast and an excellent location for a triathlon festival. Swim in the beautiful Foster Lake. Miles of low use roads wind through the hills and along the river, providing an exhilarating ride for the cyclist. Following the wooded shoreline, the run course offers relief from the summer sun. To top off your race experience, we put on an awesome post race party! We put together a HUGE BBQ with local produce just for you! After you fill up on delicious food, top it off with a couple of ice cold beers, ciders or beverages on us, and enjoy the live music and awards ceremony. With a family friendly atmosphere and races for all ages and abilities, you’ll find yourself hanging around for the whole weekend. A large, well kept campground is the final component of the equation for the ultimate triathlon festival. We hope you will join us! The Best of the West Triathlon Festival aims to promote health and fitness through a weekend of competitive and fun racing while also providing a healthy living expo where participants, volunteers and spectators will learn how to live healthier happier lives. Our goal is to help bring out the best in you! www.bestinthewesttriathlon.com

Best in the West Triathlon Festival - Designed by athletes, for athletes! Nestled in the foothills of the Cascades and fed by the Santiam River, Foster Reservoir offers premier recreation facilities to the outdoor enthusiast and an excellent location for a triathlon festival. Swim in the beautiful Foster Lake. Miles of low use roads wind through the hills and along the river, providing an exhilarating ride for the cyclist. Following the wooded shoreline, the run course offers relief from the summer sun. To top off your race experience, we put on an awesome post race party! We put together a HUGE BBQ with local produce just for you! After you fill up on delicious food, top it off with a couple of ice cold beers, ciders or beverages on us, and enjoy the live music and awards ceremony. With a family friendly atmosphere and races for all ages and abilities, you’ll find yourself hanging around for the whole weekend. A large, well kept campground is the final component of the equation for the ultimate triathlon festival. We hope you will join us! The Best of the West Triathlon Festival aims to promote health and fitness through a weekend of competitive and fun racing while also providing a healthy living expo where participants, volunteers and spectators will learn how to live healthier happier lives. Race name: Brave Run 2026
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
The Brave Run starts and ends at the Banks High School track. Participants run/walk down the main street of Banks to the Banks-Vernonia State Trail. Race continues down the Banks-Vernonia State Trail until the halfway point is reached for the 5K and 10K distance and then will head back to the starting point. Unable to participate in person? Consider registering for the virtual race. Your support is appreciated!! Register before April 27th to order a t-shirt. Limited quantities of shirts may be available for purchase day of race. Awards Every participant will receive a finisher’s medal to remember the day. Top 3 male and female finishers in the Open (overall) category Top male and female finishers in the Masters (age 40 ) category 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place ribbons awarded to the top finishers in each age group Awards will be based on official timed race results. Walkers are eligible for awards in the same categories; there are no separate walking-only divisions. Age Groups 10 & Under 11–19 20–29 30–39 40–49 50–59 60–69 70 Note: Overall (Open) and Masters award winners are not eligible for additional age group awards. The Brave Run is a benefit event for the Banks High School Parent's Association. Banks High School Parent's Association exists to provide physical and fund-raising support for athletic, extra-curricular activities and scholarships for Banks High School students.

Race name: Gator Grinder Triathlon
Listed distance: not specified
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
The North Lake Physical Therapy Gator Grinder Triathlon is an excellent introduction for the first-time triathlete, as well as a great early season event for the experienced racer. All proceeds support the Canby Gators Swim Club. Thank you for your support. Swim 500-yard (20 lengths, 10 laps) pool swim in a 6-lane, 25-yard pool, with up to 4 swimmers per lane. There will be volunteer lap counters. Drafting is permitted. The swim will be seeded by 500-yard swim-time submissions. Heat assignments will be e-mailed by the Thursday before the race. The first heat will be in the water at 7:30 a.m. Check-in at least one hour before your start. Bike The one-loop 12-mile bike course is over the beautiful rolling country roads that surround Canby. A bike helmet is mandatory. Drafting is not legal. Volunteers will manage traffic at intersections, but roads will be open to traffic and cyclists will be responsible for their safety. Run The 3.1-mile run is mostly on roadways with about one-third on a paved walking trail. The course is flat and fast. Water will be available on the course. Duathlon (run-bike-run) and Aquabike (swim-bike) Both variations will follow the same segments as the triathlon course. REGISTRATION Online registration only. All race communication is done via e-mail. Once registered, you will receive periodic informational emails. Start times will be sent the Thursday before the race. If you do not receive these emails, please check your junk or spam folders. CANCELLATIO

Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping! Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN! The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700 athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

Adoptable dogs will be on-site all day, along with food and beverage options. We will also have local vendors, and our Kids Zone with a bouncy house, face painting, and more. Every registration fuels rescue missions, lifesaving medical care, and spay/neuter clinics around the world and right here at home. To learn more, volunteer, foster, or view adoptable dogs, visit www.streetdoghero.org . Run Details Leashed, friendly dogs are welcome — bring your PAWticipant! Both races are professionally timed and run along the Deschutes River on a mix of pavement and compacted gravel with minimal elevation gain. The 5K is stroller-friendly throughout, while the 10K extends south of the Bill Healy Bridge onto a more natural, narrower stretch of trail. Every registered runner receives a custom finisher medal and complimentary beer (21 ). Race shirts and PAWticipant bandanas are available as option

The Weston Food Pantry is open for anyone who is food insecure twice each month. The Weston Food Pantry helps anyone who comes to the pantry and says that they need food, in December they served 100 families who needed food! The Weston Food Pantry doesn't care where people live, no one gets turned away. Typical food includes fruit, vegetables, canned food, dried food, bread, milk, eggs, cheese, butter and a variety of meats. Run Oregon is a locally based company whose mission is to promote opportunities in local communities to maintain an active lifestyle through organized fitness events. Community Spirit: Join a well-supported, friendly event with a vibrant atmosphere.

Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Come run or walk the Best Dam Run! This point-to-point 10K course features views of pristine waters, shading forests, interesting geology and bald eagles, osprey and colorful waterfowl. The course meanders along the wild and scenic Clackamas River for most of your journey to the downtown Estacada finish line. This event is limited to 750 entrants so don't wait and register now!

Race name: ORRC Free Member 5K Run/Walk
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
♠ ♥ ♣ ♦ Free ORRC Member Poker Run/Walk! This event is free for ORRC members who pre-register (and $25 for non-members). Everyone in the community is welcome! Come one, come all! And don't stress about an accurate distance or time! This is just a fun way to spend Labor Day holiday morning. Don't be concerned about how fast or slow you are… the only thing that matters is your poker hand! What is the Poker Run? The Poker Run/Walk is a 5K course consisting of 3 out-and-back legs all within Greenway Park in Beaverton, starting and finishing at Tractor Park The event is capped at 150 participants (due to limitations of the bike trail, and limited port-a-pottie!!! (there is only one in the park near the start area, and we are not allowed to bring in any more so... GO BEFORE YOU GO! ) If you’re not an ORRC member, you can still join the fun for a small registration fee! To find out more about the benefits of ORRC membership – click here ORRC Membership NOTE: There is no day of race registration! Event Start Times: -7:00 a.m. Registration opens -7:45 a.m. Start of the 5K Walk -8:00 a.m. Start of the 5K Run -The course will close at 10 a.m. Volunteering We’d love to have you help us put on a great event on Labor Day. If you’re interested in volunteering, please go to the volunteer tab on this page (click here - Volunteer Free Member Run ) or email race directors Julia & Tracy Reisinger at info oregonroadrunnersclub.org.

Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season. Description:

What else to expect at the race? All funds earned will be used to help Salem Harvest gather fresh produce from local farms that would go to waste and make it available for hungry families in the Willamette Valley. Haley's Heroes Foundation presents 7th Annual RUN FOR THE RARE, a 10k, 5k and 1 mile run/walk to support International Batten Disease Awareness Day. Did you know that Rare is everywhere? Join us as we run on Sunday, June 14, 2026. 1 in 10 people have a rare disease and 50% of those are children. There are more than 7000 known rare diseases and an estimated 350 million people globally diagnosed with a rare disease. YET, 95% of all rare diseases don't have a FDA approved treatment or cure. Description:
Get ready for a spine-tingling race experience at the Running Scared 5K & 13K—where thrills, chills, and fast times collide! Whether you’re brave enough to tackle the 5K or daring enough to conquer the 13K, this Halloween-themed event delivers a fun and festive atmosphere perfect for runners of all levels. Costumes are encouraged, so come dressed to impress (or frighten) as you take on a course filled with seasonal spirit. We will gather at Kiwanis Park in Eugene, OR . All athletes will receive a long-sleeve race shirt—perfect for those crisp fall mornings—and a custom finisher medal to commemorate their accomplishment. For those looking to push their limits, take on the Deadly Double by completing both the 5K and the 13K. It’s the ultimate test of endurance and Halloween courage! Competitive runners will have plenty to race for. Awards will be presented to the Top Three Male and Female Overall finishers in both the 5K and 13K, as well as the Top Three in Masters, Grand Masters, and Senior Masters Overall categories. In addition, the top three athletes in each of the traditional five-year age groups will receive awards in both race distances. For those taking on the Deadly Double, special recognition will be given to the Top Three Male and Female finishers who complete both races. Whether you’re running for fun, fitness, or a frightfully good challenge, the Running Scared 5K & 13K is sure to be a hauntingly good time you won’t want to miss!

Race name: Salem Summer Solstice 5/10K
Listed distance: 10K
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
This race is a fundraiser to support McKay HS Cross Country Team! Friday, June 12th, 2026 10k starts at 7:00 pm 5k starts at 7:10 pm Starting location: Minto Brown Island Park, parking lot #3 by the pavilion The 5K and 10K courses are flat courses in a natural setting in a beautiful park. The 5K course is all on paved trails. The 10K course does have a small loop along an open trail and then returns to a paved path again. Entry fee includes a post-race ice-cream sundae and chip timing by Eclectic Edge Racing with immediate timing results. Race divisions will be 10-year age groups (1-10, 11-20, 21-30...80-89), and the top three male/female winners will be awarded ribbons. Important Details: Restrictions: No rollerblades/skates, skateboards, dogs, or unregistered participants. Baby joggers and strollers are allowed. Walkers are welcome in the 5K. Headphones permitted as long as they allow ambient passthrough noise. Packet Pickup Begins at 6:00 pm. Day of Race Registration will end promptly at 6:50 pm & is ** all forms of payment accepted ** (unless capacity is reached before then). All race courses close at 9:00 PM. Note: Race timing and course monitoring end at 8:30 P.M. Club Member Discounts: All current members of the Willamette Valley Road Runners Club will save $3.00 on their entry fee. Join WVRR or renew today ! Aid stations: One water station is provided for both races around mile point 1.25 for the 5k and 4.25 for the 10k.

FEE: $15.00 per person if you pre-register online (before July 4th). $20.00 per person day of the race (DAY OF REGISTRATION FOR TIMED RESULTS WILL END 8:45 AM). Registration begins at 7:30 a.m. at the Stayton Community Center. INCLUDED: Ribbons to the top male and female finishers in five-year age-groups in the 5k and 10k races ; Stay around after the race to see who won the most patriotically dressed! WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED: High Entry Fees, Fancy Awards Learn More About The Race: www.StaytonFunRun.com

Sunset Bay Trail Runs feature very challenging courses, especially for the longer distances and the views will take what breath you have left away. This is an amazing, not to be missed course. Packet pickup and start/finish line is at the gazebo on far south end of Sunset Bay. Packet pickup is race morning only. Please come at least 1/2 hour before your race start time. Sunset State Park is a very gracious host and we want to keep our welcome warm. Please do not park on the grass! Half-marathoners must have reached the aid station after the first loop at Cape Arago by 10:45. This is at approximately 6.5 miles. That is an 18:28 minute mile, which is almost a fast walking pace. If you arrive at the aid station after that, we will switch you to the 15K race, no worries, you will still have a great workout and a great time! There will be water and Gatorade at the start/finish line and plenty of snacks at the finish. There is one aid station for the 15K and 1/2 marathon runners that will have water, gels, and other snacks. The 15K will pass the aid station twice and the 1/2 marathon will pass it 3 times. Description:
Celebrate the incredible strength, love, and spirit of moms everywhere at the Super Mom 5K/10K/Half Marathon! This race is all about celebrating the heroes we call “Mom”—past, present, and future. Participants can choose from the 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon distances, each designed to offer a rewarding and uplifting race-day experience. Every athlete who crosses the finish line will receive a commemorative finisher medal, a keepsake symbolizing strength, gratitude, and accomplishment. We’ll also recognize outstanding performances with awards to the top three finishers in the traditional five-year age groups, ensuring fair and exciting competition across all divisions. Come run, walk, or cheer at Kiwanis Park as we honor the incredible women who make our world better every day. It's a celebration of endurance, love, and the superpowers of moms everywhere!

Description:
REGISTRATION IS NOW OPEN!!!! Join us for this exciting fundraising event at Stickmen Brewing in Tualatin! The course is paved and mostly flat - perfect for all abilities and ages! Gather your friends, co-workers, and family to enjoy this meaningful experience together. After crossing the finish line, relax and refuel with pizza and a beverage from Stickmen Brewing. Each year, more than 4000 people in Oregon are diagnosed with breast cancer. Our mission at Breast Friends is to ensure no one goes through breast cancer alone. We strive to be relevant, accessible, and inclusive , empowering individuals to thrive beyond their diagnosis. This fundraiser directly supports our programs for individuals in your community. Registrants will be signed up for an individual fundraiser and encouraged to fundraise . Every dollar raised provides education, resources, and support to those who need it. Together, we can make a lasting impact. We are looking for photographers and a DJ with a sound system to donate their time and skills! If you or anyone you know are interested, please reach out to lizbrown breastfriends.org . Thank you!

Race name: SW Hope 5k
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
We are back again at OES in SW Portland, starting at 9:45 with kids and the 5k to follow at 10:15! Every spring, multiple Southwest Portland Faith Organizations and Community Partners join hands to meet the need of hunger specifically, by working to supply Neighborhood House’s ( https://nhpdx.org/ ) Free Food Market, the largest west of the Willamette. This joint effort is known as the Southwest Hope Campaign. Since 2016, Missio Church has organized the SW Hope 5k as a culmination of the greater campaign. What can $1 buy me at a grocery store? One, maybe two, canned goods at the most. For $1, Neighborhood House can buy 4 pounds of food directly from Oregon Food Bank. We quickly realized we could turn a simple canned food drive into a huge tool to empower Neighborhood House and reach hundreds more hungry neighbors. This is where you come in. We invite you to run with us in our annual SW Hope 5K because each $1 we raise together far outweighs it’s worth in canned goods individually. If we run together, our neighbors here in SW Portland won’t have to experience the insecurity of not knowing where their next meal is coming from.

Race name: Turtle Trot 5K, 10K, Fun Run and Brunch!
Listed distance: 10K
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Join us at Willow-Witt Ranch for The Crest’s 7th Annual Turtle Trot— a true trail race with heart (and breakfast) ! Choose the 5K or 10K on rolling single-track through meadows, wetlands, oak woodlands, and native conifer forest, or bring the whole family for a joyful Fun Run for all ages. Starting at 4,500’ and climbing to nearly 5,000’, the courses feature elevation, varied terrain, and sweeping views of Mount Shasta, Pilot Rock, and Mt. Ashland. The 10K doubles the challenge with a second lap run in reverse, ensuring you experience the views from every angle. After the finish, stay for what many say is the best part : a communal, made-from-scratch post-race breakfast shared around long tables, followed by a hands-on Western Pond Turtle learning session. Run hard, eat well, linger and learn. All proceeds support The CREST in our mission to connect people and nature.

Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
For more than 25 years, the annual USARA Adventure Race National Championships have seen some of the best teams from across the nation come together to compete in a non-stop, 30-hour adventure race. The 2026 race is limited to teams of four in three divisions: mixed gender, all-women, all-men. There is not a separate masters division, though the top masters teams from across all divisions will be recognized. Race check-in will be Thursday, October 22, 2026. The 30-hour race will start Friday morning, October 23, 2026, and end Saturday afternoon, October 24, 2026. Priority registration opens January 1, 2026. Eligible teams will receive a link by email. Open registration begins February 1, 2026. You can find the most up-to-date information on the event at the USARA website . REFUND POLICY: The RunSignUp processing fee will be deducted from any and all refunds. A racer who withdraws within one week of registering will receive a full refund, less processing fees. We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection. Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation. Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being. He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian. He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted. Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact. Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection. He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian. He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted. Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact. Listed distance: 13.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Hello Runners & Walkers! We’re excited to invite you to City Impact's 16th Annual Beachfront Run on Saturday, May 30, 2026 , at the beautiful Ventura Promenade. Enjoy a race course with stunning views of Ventura’s coastline while participating in one of our exciting race options: Half Marathon, 10K, 5K, or the Kids 1K Run. The event will also feature a variety of vendors, lively music, and a festive awards ceremony. Each participant will receive a custom event shirt and a finisher’s medal. Please note that if you register after March 15th, 2026 , we cannot guarantee your preferred shirt size. Awards will be given to the top 3 finishers in each 10-year age category (10-19, 20-29, etc.), so everyone has a chance to shine! Whether you’re racing or cheering, this is a perfect event for friends, family, and colleagues to come together and enjoy the day. All proceeds from the event will benefit City Impact’s programs supporting at-promise youth and families. Your participation makes a difference, and we thank you for your support! If you should have any questions, please email info cityimpact.com or call 805.983.3636 x105. Much appreciation, Vickie Saipale Development/Event Manager

Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
About the Event Join us on Sunday, February 28th, 2027, as the Junior Chamber International of Santa Clarita (JCI) and the Santa Clarita Track Club proudly present the 17th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K and Mini Madness 1K — benefiting JCI Santa Clarita and Students Off And Running (SOAR). SOAR provides local youth ages 14–18 with a fully supported Los Angeles Marathon training experience — completely free for participants and their families — and is an Official Featured Charity of the 2027 Los Angeles Marathon. What to Expect Mardi Gras Madness is Santa Clarita’s premier family-friendly run/walk event, offering fun and fitness for all ages! Participants will enjoy a scenic USATF-certified 5K/10K course, chip timing, custom finisher medals, marathon-quality tech shirts, and a vibrant Health & Fitness Expo. The festivities continue with a beer garden, great food, costume contest, games and giveaways, silent auction, celebrity hosts, and live entertainment. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a stroller-pusher, or bringing your furry friend, Mardi Gras Madness welcomes everyone! ‍♀️ COURSE INFORMATION The MGM course is a USATF-certified, rolling 5K/10K circuit featuring scenic paseos, bridge overpasses, and sections along the beautiful South Fork River Trail. Note: The 10K route includes a dirt equestrian trail from Mile 3.25 to Mile 4.85. EARLY PACKET PICKUP Skip the lines and pick up your race materials early! Saturday, February 27th | 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: Canyon Clu

Race name: 2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.26
Listed distance: not specified
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.25 18 EVENT OPTIONS. 6 Olympic distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 1640 Yard Swim & 10K Run), 6 Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run) and 6 Youth Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run). Triathlon = swim bike run. Typically, the swim and run distances are standard but the bike distance varies from race to race. Check out the course maps for more detailed information. CASTAIC LAKE. The 35th annual Castaic Lake Triathlon takes place at scenic Castaic Lake just 20 miles north of Los Angeles. The Castaic Lake Recreation Area, located just north of Santa Clarita, is an 11,200-acre multi-use facility with two lakes, boating, world class fishing, hiking, walking, horseback riding, wake boarding, jet-skiing, camping, picnicking, kayaking, and sailing. August is a great time to enjoy the water in the high 60s, and a staging area aptly named Paradise Cove. Tri-cation Friday night camping available through Castaic Lake. THE COURSE. The swim course is a modified V shape in Paradise Cove at Castaic Lake, with 8 lifeguards in the water on paddleboards. The bike course then goes out on back roads to limit your interaction with cars. The bike course does include some U-turns on back roads to allow this, so athletes should slow down at the turn around points. The run is primarily on the rolling trails overlooking Castaic Lake. Description:
Join us this Memorial Day for the Foothills Strong Run(formerly Fiesta Days Run), a community-powered event hosted by the YMCA of the Foothills on Monday, May 25, 2026. This meaningful day of movement and remembrance brings neighbors, families, and fitness enthusiasts together to honor resilience while supporting local families recovering from the Eaton Fire. Participants of all ages and abilities can take part in one of four unique events: the Foothills Fastest 1 Mile, Dog/Human 1 Mile, 5K Walk/Run, and the Family 1 Mile Fun Run. Whether you’re racing for a personal best, walking with friends, or running alongside your four-legged companion, there’s a place for everyone at the starting line. All events meet at Olberz Park in La Canada Flintridge. Presented by USC Verdugo Hills Hospital in partnership with the City of La Cañada Flintridge, this event goes beyond the finish line. Funds raised will provide YMCA memberships through 2026 for families impacted by the Eaton Fire — ensuring access to wellness programs, youth activities, supportive services, and a strong sense of community connection. Run, walk, and rally together — because our community is strongest when we move forward together. Event happens Rain or Shine. No Refunds.

Description:
DAM's Annual Lake Berryessa Swim is one of the longest running open water swim events in America. Started in 1981 as a friendly lake swim, this event now attracts over 500 swimmers each year to the shores of Lake Berryessa. Location: Steele Canyon Campground, Steele Canyon Road, Lake Berryessa, Napa, CA (map) Course : 1-mile and 2-mile looped courses in a freshwater lake. 1 loop for 1 mile swim, and 2 loops for 2-mile swim. See course maps at bottom of page. Host: Davis Aquatic Masters. Race Director: Kevin Waterson, berryessa damfast.org . Meet Referee: Kate Stephensen. Sanction: The adult races are sanctioned by Pacific Masters Swimming for USMS, Inc. Conditions/Safety: Expected water temperature is 68-72 degrees. Course is patrolled by safety craft. Individual escorts are not allowed. All swimmers must wear the provided swim cap and follow all USMS Open Water rules. Mandatory safety briefings will be held approximately 30 minutes prior to the start of each event. The Event Safety Plan will be posted at the registration desk on race day and is available prior to race day by request from berryessa damfast.org. Start: Deep water, wave starts (see below). Finish: Onshore. Cutoff times: For 2-mile events, 2 hours after wave start. For 1-mile events, 1 hour after wave start. Safety craft will remove swimmers who fall short of the cutoff times. Spreading Help Around You is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that was founded in 2014 in honor of Shaylyn Anela Pinoliar, who tragically passed away on November 14, 2012. Our mission is to help and support families who have lost a loved one, educate them on the importance of being prepared during such a time of loss, and provide active service to the community. As well as promoting Pedestrian Safety Awareness. This year, we proudly launched the SHAY Scholarship Program, marking an exciting new chapter in our commitment to supporting education and empowering future leaders. Each year, since Shaylyn’s passing, family, friends, and community members gather to honor her memory with an Annual 5k Run/Walk on Thanksgiving morning. Last year, we moved the event to Saturday after Thanksgiving. It was a great success, and we look forward to continuing the tradition this year to honor her memory. Run or Walk a 5K and receive an Event Shirt and a Custom Finisher's Medal. Join or Create a Team! Children 10 and under receive a special rate automatically during registration. Awards and More Age group awards for our timed 5k. First 150 Participants receive a Custom Finisher's Medal! Description:
About the Event The Tevis Cup Ride is the founding modern-day equestrian event of its kind in the world. It is seen by many as the pinnacle of the sport of equestrian endurance and is a bucket list item for many riders. The magic of the trail is strong and special, and like a siren calls those to come and take on its challenge. Therein lies the essence of the Tevis Cup Ride and the historic Western States Trail. In 2020, due to the COVID-19 Pandemic, the Western States Trail Foundation Board of Governors voted for the first time in history to cancel the annual Tevis Cup Ride. But we wanted to offer a way for our riders, crews, volunteers, supporters and lovers of the trail to still be able to participate. Thus the creation of this virtual event, which was so well received we have decided to host as an annual fundraiser. You can complete the 100-miles in as many smaller excursions as you choose to finish the goal. We absolutely recommend NOT riding the 100-miles all at once unless you are participating at an actual sanctioned event with veterinary controls. As you log your completed miles, you will receive updates of where you now are on OUR historic Western States Trail. So pick your equine partner, or register for our non-riding division, and join us for 100-miles, on YOUR own trails at your own pace . Description and Dates Register today and make your miles count! Please only count miles from AFTER you have registered, or April 23, 2026, whichever is later. The Virtual Ride

Our community energy is powerful and uplifting and we need each other more than ever so sign up early and bring a friend! One individual will receive the Finish Line Grant to assist them in their endeavours directed towards making a lasting impact on our Trans community and beyond. A Team: Create or Join a team when you register. The suggested team goal of $200! Select Volunteer to: Donate to the Silent Auction: Donate a themed basket, product or service of $20 or greater value to waive your entry fee! Participate in the Art Exhibit: Share your art (as an EDS Artist or EDS-themed art) to waive your entry fee! Event Highlights & Activities 1️⃣ Walk & Roll – One Mile (or Less!) Join our 1-mile loop at your own pace—walk, roll, or wheel! Be part of the EDS Society’s International Walk & Roll Challenge and show your dedication to raising EDS Awareness. Every step counts! 2️⃣ Silent Auction Cruise the aisles and discover treasures donated by our generous supporters. From quirky finds to one-of-a-kind items, there’s something for everyone! 3️⃣ EDS Artists’ Exhibit Marvel at art created by local EDS community members. This is your chance to see creativity, resilience, and inspiration come to life. 4️⃣ Resource & Activity Booths Explore arts & crafts, info from local providers, giveaways, hydration stations, and interactive activities

Race name: 40th Annual Tinsel Triathlon
Listed distance: not specified
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Tinsel Triathlon & 5K Reverse Sprint Pool Triathlon As one of the oldest and largest independently owned reverse sprint pool triathlons on the West Coast, it is certainly an ideal end of the season endurance race. The 35 year old event truly can be the perfect venue for Triathletes of all levels. For first timers who have always wanted to be triathletes the course is well defined, attainable and loaded with helpful volunteers. We are also an awesome setting for the seasoned triathlete. The course layout lets you push yourself hard for a solid workout. What better way to get your game on ... Reverse Sprint Pool Triathlon! The Tinsel is a Sunday Triathlon run on a usually sunny, yet crisp, Southern California day with all roads closed and the coffee hot. The 5K run takes place in a scenic, calm area of West Hemet, California in Riverside County. Known as a flat & fast course, the 12 mile bike ride gives the rider a feeling of being on the country roadside. The race ends in the 25 meter heated pool at West Valley High School , triathletes will swim 150 meters (up & back 6 times) to the finish line where you receive a unique Tinsel finisher medal. The awards ceremony follows immediately and the bling is top shelf!

Created to bring more running events—and more mile races—to the South Bay San Diego community, this event welcomes runners of all ages, speeds, and experience levels. Inspired by Mexican heritage and the Battle of Puebla, La Batalla de las Millas blends culture, competition, and community into a unique Cinco de Mayo running experience—because every mile deserves to be celebrated.

Race name: 6th Annual Viva Frida 50 Mile Challenge
Listed distance: 50 Miles
Listed difficulty: Extreme

Description:
“Viva Frida” 50-Mile Challenge- A Journey of Strength, Art, and Self-Love This July, take on the “Viva Frida” 50-Mile Challenge, a tribute to the bold, brilliant, and resilient spirit of Frida Kahlo . Known for transforming pain into art and embracing her true self with fearless authenticity, Frida continues to inspire generations to rise above, express freely, and walk through life with courage. Why 50 Miles? Every mile symbolizes Frida’s powerful voice, vibrant creativity, and unbreakable strength. Whether you walk, run, bike, or move in your own way—let each mile reflect your journey of self-expression, healing, and empowerment. Challenge Dates: July 1 – July 31, 2026 How to Join: 1. Register online 2. Choose your activity (walk, run, jog, hike) —mix it up! 3. Track your miles throughout the month. 4. Share your progress on social media using #VivaFridaChallenge 5. Complete your 50 miles and receive your commemorative medal, tech-tee and waterproof sticker! Bonus: Wear bold colors, flowers in your hair, or anything inspired by Frida’s iconic style as you complete your miles. Dedicate your challenge to a cause, a personal transformation, or to reclaiming your power—just as Frida did through every brushstroke. Let’s celebrate her legacy by moving with intention, loving fiercely, and living colorfully. Viva la vida. Viva Frida!

Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Roger's Race (Walk & Run 5K) is a free event open to the public. It is a partnered event put on by Modesto Moves Training Team and Faith Home Adult & Teen Challenge (FHTC) located at 6643 Faith Home Road, Ceres. This is a fun run; however, a timing clock and timing chips will be used this year. Awards given for overall 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finishers. Modesto Moves Training Team sponsors the race by providing race guidance and runners/walkers to the event. We also donate 100% of all proceeds collected by the Moves organization to Faith Home Teen Challenge. FHTC is a faith based recovery program reaching out to men to show them how to get their lives back through a faith based concept. Whether you are faith based or not, there is a positive impact to the local community with the work that is being done at FHTC. Roger's Run was a dream of Roger Williams, a Modesto Moves walker, who passed away suddenly in July of 2017. Modesto Moves, along with FHTC, made the dream a reality in 2018. Roger's Run is his legacy to FHTC where he worked until the time of his death. The event will include a pancake breakfast provided by FHTC (suggested $5/person donation), drawing prizes (no cost, bib number is your entry) and raffle prizes (tickets sold by Modesto Moves).

Race name: Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run
Listed distance: 50 Miles
Listed difficulty: Extreme

Description:
The Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run is the oldest Ultra Trail Run in California with the 50 Mile run entering its 44th year. The 50K joined the party seven years ago and instantly became a California classic in trail running traversing all of the same trails that the older run uses. Running the Avalon Benefit 50Mile/50K provides you a first rate, up-close and personal experience of one of California's natural jewels in trail running across Catalina Island. The run begins and ends in Avalon and in between you simply have to run the entire length of the island - and back! In between you will experience beautiful vistas, tremendous views of the Pacific Ocean, see a bison or two and experience some of the sports great volunteers and aid stations.

There is a total elevation gain of over 9000 feet (2740m). The twelve previous editions were received with wide acclaim. The thirteenth edition – with a limit of 100 runners – is scheduled for April 18-19 (Saturday-Sunday), 2026. Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
2026 ATHLETE GUIDE CLICK HERE BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE A Gravel Ride experience you don't want to miss. Choose your ride experience around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic ride in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests. BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike GRAVEL RIDE 36K t akes you ONE LOOP around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Great for your first Gravel/Off-Road Ride GRAVEL RIDE 72K takes you TWO LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Test your skills and make it a double. GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 108K takes you THREE LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Find your limits and test your endurance. GRAVEL YOUTH 10K is a fun and flat fun ride for the spirited rider/beginner. An out and back course that gets you stoked! NEW! GRAVEL KID'S 3k fun ride. Parents ride with your kids and get them on the dirt. For Kid's 10 and under. TEAM CHALLENGE enjoy the ride with friends and complete laps as a team in the 72k and 108k.

Description:
Big Sur River Run is a benefit race for two important Big Sur community organizations, Big Sur Health Center and Big Sur Fire. There are two races, a 10k and 5k. Both courses are all flat, black-top road loops alongside Big Sur River, through Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park's redwood and oak grove campgrounds. The 10k is a certified course. The 5k is a Family Fun Run or Walk. No Bicycles, dogs, strollers, skates, wagons, or other wheeled conveyances (other than wheelchairs) are permitted. Prizes for 10K Race winners and top finishers. Since 1981 two of Big Sur’s most vital institutions have been supported by the generosity of those who love to run. Most who visit Big Sur revel in the remoteness without taking in the impact it has on emergency services. The local Volunteer Fire Department, Big Sur Fire, and the Big Sur Health Center both rely on donations to provide support for visitors and residents alike. The run’s beneficiaries, Big Sur Fire and the Big Sur Health Center, have never done more to serve and support our community than in recent years. These critical emergency services need our support more than ever and we encourage you to donate to each organization directly. To date over 30,000 runners have joined the cause, supporting these institutions, and basking in the beauty of Big Sur. Will you join us this year?

The local Volunteer Fire Department, Big Sur Fire, and the Big Sur Health Center both rely on donations to provide support for visitors and residents alike. The run’s beneficiaries, Big Sur Fire and the Big Sur Health Center, have never done more to serve and support our community than in recent years. These critical emergency services need our support more than ever and we encourage you to donate to each organization directly. To date over 30,000 runners have joined the cause, supporting these institutions, and basking in the beauty of Big Sur. Will you join us this year?

Race name: Bike Hut Classic
Listed distance: 8.3 Miles
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
It's beautiful...it's challenging...it's a bucket-list Bay Area ride through Coastal Redwoods for a great cause! Rally your club members or friends for this annual DIY ride, to be completed on your own from July 3 - 19. Set out from the iconic Bike Hut rest stop (a world famous cycling treasure), rolling down Tunitas Creek Road through coastal farms and scenic countryside before starting the ascent through the Redwoods with switchbacks and stunning forest views. Climb 1900 feet in elevation and 8.3 miles to Skyline Boulevard, all while supporting Abundant Grace Coastside Worker! Make it an out-and-back from the top or bottom of Tunitas...or add it to a larger ride from over the hill or up the Coast. One hundred percent of proceeds go to Abundant Grace as we hire the homeless community to work at Potrero Nuevo Farm (behind the Bike Hut). The organic produce is donated to low-income families, and participants earn money while giving back to the community. Registration includes a limited edition t-shirt and entry to our Ride Reception on Saturday, July 25 with ice cream sundaes, podium photos, and live music. Top riders earn prizes and get their name on a plaque inside the Bike Hut, as will the bike club that raises the most funds.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and takes the outbound portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 4 miles to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. Black women and birthing people are 3-4 times more likely to die from pregnancy related causes and complications than their white counterparts. Most pregnancy related deaths are preventable. Multiple factors contribute to these disparities, such as structural racism, implicit bias, variation in quality healthcare, and underlying chronic conditions. It is a week of awareness, advocacy, activism, and collaboration​ to amplify ​the voices, perspectives and lived experiences of Black Mamas and birthing people. Black women and birthing people are 3-4 times more likely to die from pregnancy related causes and complications than their white counterparts. Most pregnancy related deaths are preventable. Multiple factors contribute to these disparities, such as structural racism, implicit bias, variation in quality healthcare, and underlying chronic conditions. Social determinants of health have historically prevented many people from racial and ethnic minority groups from having fair opportunities for economic, physical, and emotional health. Black Maternal Health Week (BMHW) was founded and is led by Black Mamas Matter Alliance . BMHW takes place annually from April 11-17 and was recognized by the White House on April 13, 2021. It is a week of awareness, advocacy, activism, and collaboration​ to amplify ​the voices, perspectives and lived experiences of Black Mamas and birthing people. This year's theme is Rooted in Justice & Joy . Purpose: To raise awareness, promote activism, and amplify community-driven, Reproductive Justice-centered care. Welcome to the 16th edition of the Boogie Nights Summer Run Series presented by the Ventura Running Club. We highly recommend you register in advance which will speed up the check-in process. You can sign up on-site each week for $17 (plus a processing fee that goes to the registration company) All Series 5K participants will get a free Boogie Nights Event Shirt and will have the option during registration to add on a meal/ drink. Individual Night Sign-ups can pre-purchase a shirt or meal/drink. A great way to get in shape and have fun while raising money for the local High School Cross Country Teams. Over the past 11 years we have raised over $50,000 for the program. Last year we raised close to $10,000. When? Every Wednesday Night from May 20th - July 22nd Kids 1K - 6:00PM 5K - 6:20PM Check-In & Race Day Registration - 5:15pm - 6:15pm Where? The Ventura Promenade starting in front of Aloha Steakhouse and The Crowne Plaza. Course Map: https://www.plotaroutehttps://www.plotaroute.com/route/2946249?units=miles Parking - PLEASE DO NOT PARK in the lot next to Aloha Steakhouse. That parking lot has had damage and has very limited parking and we want to leave that available for customers of Aloha Steakhouse, Crown Plaza, and Beach House Fish. We would recommend parking in the free City lot

Race name: Bruin Run/Walk 5K
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Bruin Run/Walk is excited to present the 26th annual 5K at UCLA, benefiting The Painted Turtle. This year's theme is SLUMBER PARTY RUN! Make sure to show up in your best pajamas, and we highly recommend bringing a stuffed Teddy Bear or other plushie along for the ride! As one of twelve committees within UCLA’s USAC Student Wellness Commission (SWC), Bruin Run/Walk organizes one of the largest student-run events on campus each year. ​ The Bruin Run/Walk 5K supports the The Painted Turtle, a camp in Lake Hughes, California for children with chronic illnesses and their families. The 5k event brings together nearly 1000 students, UCLA faculty, and members of the greater LA community in support of this meaningful cause. ​ For 25 years, Bruin Run/Walk has been a proud UCLA tradition, raising over $75,000 for our beneficiary! This event is made possible by a dedicated team of UCLA undergraduate students working closely with The Painted Turtle.

Description:
Experience the ultimate California trail half-marathon, an adventure that will test your limits while rewarding you with awe-inspiring beauty. Starting in the charming town of Avalon, the race kicks off with a scenic run past the historic Wrigley Mansion. From there, you’ll journey into Catalina Island’s rugged Interior, tackling challenging climbs that lead to breathtaking peaks. At the summit, take in sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean, where, on a clear day, you might catch a glimpse of two other Channel Islands. The journey continues with a thrilling descent through the serene Wrigley Memorial, winding your way back into the heart of Avalon. For runners looking for a shorter, yet equally stunning course, the 10K route offers a picturesque tour through Avalon’s scenic hillsides, capturing the island’s unique charm and natural beauty. Whether you’re taking on the half-marathon or the 10K, this race is a perfect blend of challenge, adventure, and unforgettable views.

Race name: Champion Mine Trail Race
Listed distance: 13.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Challenge Yourself and Enjoy the Great Outdoors Join the Sierra TrailBlazers Running Club and Bear Yuba Land Trust for the inaugural Champion Mine Trail Race! Get ready to travel to a must-see destination race in Northern California. Explore some of Nevada City’s most exciting trails with this brand-new half-marathon (13.1 miles) event. The course winds through towering pines, crosses a historic swinging bridge, and challenges runners with a series of rewarding climbs. With multiple aid stations, historical landmarks, and a newly constructed trail section offering varied terrain, this course rivals some of the best trail races in Northern California. Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line! The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

Race name: Chester 4th of July Fun Run
Listed distance: 1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
One mile route down historic Chester Main Street! The Almanor Recreation and Park District’s 45th annual Chester 4th of July Fun Run will take place at 9 a.m. on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The one mile run/walk will start on the Collins Pine lawn located at 500 Main Street and proceed down Chester’s historic Main Street to the finish at the Bidwell House located at 1 Main Street. Participants will receive a commemorative T-shirt (first 400 registrants) and enjoy refreshments at the finish line. After the event, there will be a 4th of July Craft Fair at Chester Park from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and a 4th of July Parade starting at 11 a.m. on Main Street. The Craft Fair is sponsored by the Chester Elks and the Parade is sponsored by the Lake Almanor Area Chamber of Commerce. The one mile route down Main Street is open to participants of all ages and abilities, and adds to the excitement of the 4th of July celebration in town. The Fun Run is ARPD's largest fundraising event and all proceeds benefit District programs and events, as well as capital improvement projects, with an emphasis on recreation, parks and trails. Please join us this year for a great time and be sure to wear your favorite costume or sport your 4th of July colors and bling. Spectators are also welcome. Thanks for your support!

Race name: Chico Air Museum RUN THE RUNWAY! 5K and One Mile Run/Walk
Listed distance: 1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Do you feel the need? The need for speed?! If you do then this timed 1 mile run on the main runway at the Chico Regional Airport is the event for you. Or, if you want a longer race, choose the 5K option with the first mile on the runway. The Chico Air Museum is a 501(c)(3) non-profit aviation and space museum located at the Chico Regional Airport. The museum is open to the public Thursdays-Sundays and charges no admission. Numerous aircraft and historical exhibits are on display, both indoors and outdoors. Volunteer docents are available to provide tours and explain the rich aviation history of Chico and Northern California. RUN THE RUNWAY! is a timed mile and 5K for runners, joggers, and walkers which takes place on Runway 31R at the Chico Regional Airport. This is a rare and unique opportunity to run on an actual aircraft runway. Overall and age group medals will be awarded. The race ends at the Chico Air Museum which will be open to visitors following the race. Museum admission is always free. Please come out and enjoy this special event. Thank you for supporting the Chico Air Museum. Please Note: Runners who register after March 20th are not guaranteed a shirt. Please register in advance. There will be no race day registration.

Race name: Chico Air Museum RUN THE RUNWAY! 5K and One Mile Run/Walk
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Do you feel the need? The need for speed?! If you do then this timed 1 mile run on the main runway at the Chico Regional Airport is the event for you. Or, if you want a longer race, choose the 5K option with the first mile on the runway. The Chico Air Museum is a 501(c)(3) non-profit aviation and space museum located at the Chico Regional Airport. The museum is open to the public Thursdays-Sundays and charges no admission. Numerous aircraft and historical exhibits are on display, both indoors and outdoors. Volunteer docents are available to provide tours and explain the rich aviation history of Chico and Northern California. RUN THE RUNWAY! is a timed mile and 5K for runners, joggers, and walkers which takes place on Runway 31R at the Chico Regional Airport. This is a rare and unique opportunity to run on an actual aircraft runway. Overall and age group medals will be awarded. The race ends at the Chico Air Museum which will be open to visitors following the race. Museum admission is always free. Please come out and enjoy this special event. Thank you for supporting the Chico Air Museum. Please Note: Runners who register after March 20th are not guaranteed a shirt. Please register in advance. There will be no race day registration.

The Citrus Heritage Run is an experience you won’t want to miss!

Race name: Coronado Rotary Low Tide Ride & Stride
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Celebrate the 29th Anniversary of the Low Tide Ride & Stride with a our 5K Course during the lowest tide of the month on the beach from North Beach down to the end of the Shores and back. Kick off summer with this fun, family-friendly, 5K chip-timed race. Run! Walk! Bike! Stroll! This Coronado signature event takes place along one of the top 10 beaches in the world and provides much needed funds with Local Military and First Responders being the primary beneficiaries. Drop your beach chair in Sunset Park along with your reusable water bottle. After the race, kick back and enjoy LIVE MUSIC, grab a snack, visit local vendors' booths, and more. WHY THE 5K COURSE? If you have participated in past Low Tide Ride & Stride events, you may have noticed military and civilian volunteers lining the beach along the State Park and Navy Base. They were protecting the Least Tern’s nesting grounds. You see, the Least Terns are an endangered species and their numbers continue to dwindle. Even the military must limit their training on the beach during nesting season March – September. According to the Audubon Society, since 1970 we have lost half of all bird populations globally. By keeping the course of the race off of the Amphibious Base, Rotary is protecting critical nesting grounds for the Least Tern and Snowy Plover. We are excited for race course -- less hassle, family friendly, and fun at Sunset Park! We can’t think of a better way to bike, run, walk and celebrate the beginning of summer

Viva La Vida 5K, 10K & Half Marathon Sunday, November 1 | Long Beach, CA Start/Finish: 5400 E Ocean Blvd Celebrate life, honor those who came before us, and run your heart out at our Day of the Dead-inspired race by the beach. It's an Orange County tradition! The Dinosaur Dash is a community run, walk, and bike event benefiting the Tustin Public Schools Foundation. There's something for everyone--a 2k fun run, chip-timed 5k and 10k runs, and Bike Tours for all riding levels (15k and a family-friendly 5k). The finisher medal for the 10k, 5k, and Bike Tour features our unique, student-designed logo. The 5k and 10k top finishers in each racing age division will receive the official Dino Dash trophy--hand-made by Tustin Unified students. Second- and third-place finishers will receive a medal. The 2k Fun Run and the Bike Tour are not timed and do not have age division awards. The 15k bike tour passes through Tustin and Irvine before returning to The Market Place in Tustin. This tour is recommended for riders age 13 and up since it is on open roads. We also offer a family-friendly 5K tour on closed roads. The Bike Tours are not timed. A free family Expo will offer activities, school fundraising booths, and exhibitors. The Tustin Public Schools Foundation is a charitable organization that supports the students and teachers of Tustin Unified schools by funding grants, scholarships, and enrichment programs such as after-school sports, robotics, college readiness, Tustin Summer Academy, and more. PLEASE NOTE: Race day registrations (Sunday, November 2nd) do not include a shirt. Description:
Join us for a day of fun and fitness at the third annual Dream Big 5k, proudly presented by the Kiwanis Club of Victorville. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun walk with friends and family, this event promises an enjoyable experience for participants of all levels. The race takes you through the scenic paths of Victor Valley College, located at 18422 Bear Valley Rd, Victorville, CA, starting bright and early at 8:00 am on Saturday, August 22. But the fun doesn't end at the finish line! Stick around for a variety of race day activities, including local vendors, lively music, and more. Every stride you take helps us support students in the Victor Valley, driving the change we wish to see in our community. Grab your running shoes, and let’s make dreams come true together at the Dream Big 5k! After the main Dream Big 5K, stick around for even more fun—our Dream Big Mini K for children ages 12 and under! Held at Victor Valley College, this in-person event is all about encouraging kids to get active, dream big, and feel proud of their accomplishments. It’s a joyful, high-energy experience where little ones can cross the finish line to the cheers of friends and family. The first 50 registered participants of the Mini K will receive a special finisher medal—so don’t wait to sign up! Let’s make it a day to remember filled with smiles, movement, and celebration. Come cheer them on and help create a lasting memory at the Dream Big Mini K!

Race name: Ely Mountain Trail Race
Listed distance: 8.7 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Ely Mountain Trail Race – Shaver Lake, CA 14K (8.7mi) 8K (4.9mi) | Balsam Forebay | Cooler temps. Hot trails. We’re stoked to bring a brand new adventure to the San Joaquin Running Co lineup — and this one’s a beauty. Join us in the mountains above Shaver Lake for the first-ever Ely Mountain Trail Race, where crisp air, big climbs, and epic views are all on the menu. The 14K course brings the heat with about 1,800 feet of climbing, including a 1,000’ ascent up Ely Mountain. You’ll earn sweeping views of the Sierra, Shaver Lake, and the valley below — then fly down some smooth and fast singletrack and dirt roads back to the finish. The 8K hits a slightly easier route to the top but still climbs about 800 feet, with all the mountain vibes and finish line feels. ️ Special Award for King & Queen of the Mountain – fastest segment times to the top of Ely! Custom race shirts Finisher medals podium awards Post-race food refreshments All the crisp mountain air you’ve been missing We’re capping this one at 250 runners, so don’t sleep on it — grab your spot and come break in these trails with us.

Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Fit, Black, and Educated, Inc. JUNETEENTH 5K San Diego RUN IT - WALK IT - CELEBRATE FREEDOM Join us in San Diego for the 2026 FBE Juneteenth 5K Run/Walk. Move with purpose. Celebrate freedom. Join us as we run, walk, or roll together in honor of Juneteenth and the generations who fought for liberation. Together we move to improve our health, honor our ancestors, and strengthen the future of our community. The FBE Juneteenth 5K is an annual community race hosted by Fit, Black, and Educated, Inc. (FBE) . Juneteenth commemorates June 19, 1865, when Union General Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston, Texas and announced that enslaved people were free—more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation. Today, Juneteenth is recognized as a commemoration and celebration of family, liberation, heritage, unity, and resilience. Through movement, the FBE Juneteenth 5K brings our community together to celebrate this important history while promoting health, wellness, and unity. Participants of all fitness levels are welcome to run, walk, or roll.

Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
2026 registration will open April 3. -------------------------- Join us for our 15th Annual Folsom Firecracker on Saturday, 2026, July 4th. This community-oriented event is a fun and healthy way to kick off the 4th of July before your festivities with family and friends. The 2 Mile, 5K, and 10K races are timed events that travel primarily along the paved paths of the Lake Natoma bike trails and overlook the American River. The Kids Fun Run is a 1/4 Mile non-competitive race for ages 10 and younger. Finishers of all races will receive a medal upon completion. Overall and age group awards are presented in all three timed races. In the 5K and 10K, we have unique special divisions and awards to recognize adaptive athletes, Folsom residents, first responders, active military and veterans, cancer survivors and stroller entrants. Post-race, enjoy complimentary sno-cones, refreshments, and vendor booths. We hope to see you there! Event Details: Registration for the 2 Mile, 5K, and 10K includes a race t-shirt, chip timing, eligibility for age group & special division awards (5K/10K), and a finisher's medal. Kids Fun Run: The Kids Run will be approximately 1/4 a mile and will be held at 9:00am. Open to kids ages 10 and Under. Entry includes a bib number and finisher medal (race is not timed). A t-shirt may be added to the entry for $5. One parent may run alongside each child in the Kids Run if this makes the child more comfortable (parent does not need to register). Kids who are regist

Race name: Footsteps for Families
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Join us for Footsteps for Families, a community‑driven 5K run/walk and Kids 1K fun run supporting the Safe Families AV Chapter—held on the Saturday of Mother’s Day weekend. This special timing gives us the beautiful opportunity to honor and support mothers in our community, especially those facing the toughest seasons of life. By participating, you’re helping provide stability, encouragement, and practical support to moms who are working hard to keep their families safe and strong. Footsteps for Families invites runners, walkers, families, and neighbors of all ages and abilities. Whether you’re aiming for a personal record, enjoying a leisurely stroll, or cheering on your little ones in the Kids 1K, you’ll be part of a warm, family‑friendly event featuring community partners, activities for children, and opportunities to learn about the mission of Safe Families. All proceeds directly benefit the Safe Families AV Chapter , helping provide temporary hosting, mentorship, and wraparound support to families in crisis—ensuring children remain safe, supported, and with their parents. Your participation is truly a gift to local mothers who need a strong community behind them. Highlights: • All runners receive a custom finishers medal • 5K Run / Walk registrations receive race T-Shirt • **FREE** PROFESSIONAL PICTURES TAKEN DAY OF RACE! • Timed 5K run/walk • Kids 1K fun run • Family‑friendly activities and community engagement • Supports local families in crisis through Safe Families A

Description:
Celebrate Independence Day at the Fresno Freedom Run this July 4th as we mark the 250th anniversary of our nation! Start your holiday with a memorable run or walk along an American flag–lined course, surrounded by community spirit and patriotic pride. The event features a 4-mile run/walk, a 2-mile run/walk, and a fun Kids Run to kick off the morning’s festivities, making it the perfect way for runners, walkers, and families of all ages to participate. Participants will receive a participant shirt, chip timing, post-race snacks, and a newly designed commemorative finisher medal (design coming in April). Most importantly, your participation helps support Central Valley Honor Flight, an organization dedicated to honoring local World War II, Korean War, and Vietnam War veterans by sending them to Washington, D.C. to visit the memorials built in their honor. Gather your friends and family and start your Fourth of July with a run that celebrates freedom, community, and those who served.

Description:
League of Mexican American Women warmly invites you to be a part of something special—the 5th Annual Frida Fun Run! This beloved event celebrates community, fitness, culture, and is an opportunity to raise scholarship funds for local students. Since this is our fifth year, we're celebrating our own “ Cinco-ñera ” marking five years of bringing the central valley community together. Our aim this year is to bolster our scholarship program, increasing the number of scholarships awarded to students. Join us for a day filled with friends, family, fun, and fitness! Held on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at Fresno City College, the event takes place on a vibrant, picturesque campus in the heart of Fresno. With its lush green spaces, historic buildings, and tree-lined walkways, the setting beautifully reflects the spirit of community and cultural pride. Join us and help us empower the next generation through education! About the League of Mexican American Women (LMAW) Founded in 1973 in Fresno County, the League of Mexican American Women (LMAW) is a grassroots organization dedicated to empowering our community through education, cultural celebration, leadership development, and service. Discover our programs and how you can get involved here .

Description:
Raising Awareness and Funds for Frontotemporal Degeneration We are excited to announce the FTD Walk for Hope 5K , a community event dedicated to raising awareness and funds for Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) , a devastating brain disorder that affects behavior, language, and personality. Unlike Alzheimer’s disease, FTD often strikes people in their 40's to 60's, leading to profound changes in relationships, work, and independence. There is currently no cure, and increased awareness and research funding are crucial. Our walk supports the Association for Frontotemporal Degeneration (AFTD) , a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. The FTD Walk for Hope 5K mission is to unite the community and honor those affected by FTD. All proceeds from this event will be donated to support The Association for Frontotemporal Degeneration's (AFTD) mission. Funds will be designated 50% towards AFTD's FTD Research efforts and 50% towards AFTD's Comstock Grants, which provides financial assistance to families affected by FTD. Any unspent California-designated funds as of June 30, 2026, will be redirected to support individuals diagnosed with FTD or their caregivers in other states. Together, we can bring hope to families and move on step closer to a future free of FTD.” Details for the FTD Walk for Hope 5K: Event date: Saturday, April 11, 2026 Registration check-in will open at 9:00 AM Program will begin at 9:30 AM with a Welcome Address followed by the 5K fun walk Thank you for consider

Race name: Full Moon Gauntlet
Listed distance: 22 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
As the sunsets and the full moon begins to rise over the desert, you begin an epic journey across what looks like moonscape, over a far away peak only to summit to one of the tallest peaks in SoCal. Now begins your starlit quest to do epic shit. Friday night, May 1st at 9pm we step off into the desert under a full moon and we don’t stop until it’s done. We’re hosting a one of a kind overnight full moon hike deep in the Anza Borrego Desert. No crowds, no noise, just you, the moon, and a mountain most people will never even attempt. We’re keeping the peak a secret for a reason. What I will tell you is this… it’s considered one of the toughest hikes in San Diego County. Roughly 22 miles round trip with over 8000 feet of elevation gain. Rugged, dry, unforgiving terrain. Barely a trail. Less than 100 people a year even touch it. This is not a casual stroll. This is a gut check. You’ll climb through the night under a full moon, push past doubt, and earn a sunrise most people will never see. No shortcuts, no hand holding, just grit, mindset, and a crew that shows up ready. And here’s the deal… this is the only overnight full moon hike we’re doing this year. You miss it, you miss it. If you’ve been looking for something different, something raw, something that actually challenges you… this is it. Spots are limited. Step up or sit this one out. NOTE: Gut Check Fitness, LLC policy is that there are NO REFUNDS and/or TRANSFERS. You are making a commitment to train, work hard, stay focus

The Gold Rush Adventure Challenge: Dawn to Dusk is a 12 hour adventure challenge set in one of the most spectacular landscapes run the world: San Francisco Bay Area. For complete details, visit our website ( link ) Starting in the charming small town of Sausalito, teams will navigate by map and compass (no GPS!) through the dramatic terrain of the Marin Headlands, paddle the waters of the San Francisco Bay, and explore the historic trails of Angel Island. Racers will move through a landscape defined by steep coastal ridges, ocean cliffs, historic military sites, and sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the skyline of San Francisco. Teams of 1 to 4 racers will trek, mountain bike, and paddle between checkpoints spread across the course. Each team receives a map and must choose how to navigate the terrain and collect checkpoints within the 12 hour time limit. A central transition area in Sausalito allows teams to return to race headquarters between disciplines to change gear, regroup, and plan their next leg before heading back out on course. The race is designed to be approachable for first time adventure racers while still offering meaningful strategy and physical challenge for experienced teams . Navigation is straightforward enough for newcomers to learn the sport while the terrain and route choices reward strong teamwork and efficient movement. This event will be EPIC! Race name: Graniterock River Run
Listed distance: not specified
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Please join us for the River Run back for a great 6th year in 2026. A family-friendly event that will be fun for everyone! You'll be able to run or walk a 5K distance or a 1Mile untimed fun run. The River Run 2026 is a unique experience that meanders through a working sand and gravel quarry. The events take you inside the Southside Sand and Gravel Quarry to see the working quarry site, the banks of the San Benito River, specialized equipment that processes the rock, and beautiful natural surroundings. River Run benefits the YMCA of San Benito County and begins promptly at 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 12th 2026. Check in begins at 7:00am. Pricing is available for individuals or families. The family pricing option is available for families/groups of 4 or more participants. The event is located the the Graniterock Sand and Gravel Quarry at 5632 Airline Highway, Hollister, CA 95023. Free parking is available at the race site.
