Description:
Join us for the Griffith Park Trail Marathon Relay & 8K, an unforgettable race experience celebrated as one of Runner’s World magazine’s 10 Best Races You’ve Never Heard Of in 2024! This iconic event is the perfect opportunity to push yourself, bond with friends, and take in the breathtaking beauty of Griffith Park. With a combination of scenic trails and challenging terrain, you’ll be in for the ride of your life. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just starting out, join us for a solo run or bring a team for a relay. And with fully-stocked aid stations and an energetic volunteer crew, you’ll have everything you need to crush it. So come on, grab your running shoes, and let’s make this a moment to remember! Register now for a day of adventure, camaraderie, and lasting memories. One of the largest urban parks in the country, Griffith Park is a 4,300-plus acre slice of runner heaven. The grounds include famous sites like the Abandoned Los Angeles Zoo, the Observatory, and the Hollywood Sign. There’s more than 30 trails totaling around 50 miles for runners and hikers. Join us for the Griffith Park Trail Relay Marathon and get a taste of what the second largest city park has to offer. All participants will receive a premium short sleeve women's or men's cut t-shirt. (Guaranteed shirt size if you register by May 17!) Relay run is chip timed for fast & accurate results. $1500 in Cash prizes for the Open division Trophy/Plaque for the top 3 teams in each recreational division Fini

Obviously the dirt sections of the gravel routes see almost zero vehicles, but the paved route also see very few cars! So wheather you choose the grueling Century with it’s 10,000’ of elevation gain, gorgeous views of Eagles Beak, Globe Rock, or Mile High overlook as you climb up to Beasore Meadows, or if you choose the Gravel Route it’s 60 miles 6,000’ of gain up Central Camp Rd through the lush forest, which also climbs to Beasore, you’ll no doubt be treated to expansive views of lakes, numerous granite domes, & many lush meadows. If you want your day to be a bit easier, the paved road riders can do the Metric Century, which climbs the same road as the regular century, but is simply a 22 mile OAB to North Fork, then a CCW loop around Bass Lake. Gravel riders opting for an easier day can follow the main Gravel ride up Central Camp Rd, do a “lollipop loop” merging back onto Central Camp & descend back down to Bass Lake. PARTICIPANT PERKS All registered participants receive: ✔ Official event T-shirt ✔ Custom H2GO 5K finisher

If you want to participate in the event without your child, take advantage of our $8 per child - child care for children ages 3 and up! We will have a post race pancake breakfast. The Heart of Cool Trail Run traverses some of the best trails Cool, CA and the Sierra Foothills have to offer. Run on the same trails as many of the famous local (and world renowned) events such as Western States 100 Mile, Way too Cool 50k, Rio Del Lago 100 Mile, and many more! Race name: Heartfelt Fun & Run
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Heartfelt Help Foundation is hosting our fourth annual virtual 5k! Hike, bike, run, walk, swim or dance! However you move, move with us and raise needed funds to help heart transplant recipients right here in Northern California pay for the costs associated with transplant that insurance doesn't cover. This includes our lodging program, providing temporary recovery housing when their doctors require it, their insurance doesn't cover it, and they can't afford it, and our new program, Axel's Helping Hand to help heart transplant patients and their families in Northern California with costs that are non-medical, but patients and families are unable to pay due to loss of income related to their transplant. This includes overdue rent, car payments, utilities and much more. We believe that financial stability leads to family stability which ultimately leads to the health of the patient and longevity of their new heart. HHF ensures Equity and Access for heart transplant recipients despite their personal financial limitations providing what is necessary to facilitate recovery, and helps patients return them home as soon and as strong as possible. Join us today wherever you are and let's move to provide help and hope for financially disadvantaged heart transplant patients! Heartfelt Help Foundation is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in good standing. All donations over and above the event registration fee are fully tax deductible to the extent allowed by law. RACE START TIME: 7:00 AM WHAT MAKES THIS RACE STAND OUT: 2nd Race - Run The Valley Half Marathon Series 11 AID STATIONS - L oaded with Ice, Water, Sponges, Gatorade, GU's, AND A LOT OF FUN! Yes, that's FREE too! Michelob Ultra Stage It's a Party in the Park Top 3 Age Group & Relay Awards Overall Male/Female Awards Top Relay Awards (3 Divisions) Women's Tech Tank Top Men's (Unisex) Short-Sleeve Tech Shirt PRO~PT at the Finish Line for your Post Race Awesome Finishers Medal

Race name: Heroes 4 Hearing 5K
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Avoid lines on race day: Pick Up Your Bib and shirt on Saturday August 16th at Sports Basement from 11am to 1pm. Place Shoreline Aquatic Park 200 Aquarium Way, Long Beach, CA 90802 HearAid Foundation presents our 4th Annual Heroes for Hearing 5K Fundraiser. Be inspired by heroes overcoming their hearing loss. Run with heroes who bring the gift of hearing. Become a hero. Join us on Sunday, August 17th on the water front, behind the aquarium, in Long Beach, California (or virtually) as we celebrate our recipients and those who helped give the gift of hearing! Let’s run and walk together so we can keep on giving this precious gift. All participants who register by July 25th are guaranteed to receive a t-shirt, and ALL participants are guaranteed to have lots of fun! Join us for an exhilarating run through the marina and along the shore with views of the Queen Mary in Long Beach, California. Whether you're up for a 5k or the Kids Run, this event promises a memorable experience amidst the natural beauty of the shoreline. Event Details: Location: Shoreline Aquatic Park, 200 Aquarium Way, Long Beach, CA 90802 Bib Pickup: Starts at 7 am Race Start Times: 5k: 8:00 am Kids Dash : 9:15 am Parking Available a short walk away at the multi-level aquarium parking lot. Fees in the lot are by the hour, click this link for more details. Course Map: https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6274860286/ Course Description: The race starts and ends behind the aquarium, next to Pierpont Landing. 5k run

Description:

Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Hobby Joggers organizes FUN RUN events designed to be high-energy and genuinely welcoming. Our races celebrate participation over placement, with Signature Anti-awards that recognize effort, spirit, creativity, and showing up, not just who finishes first. Every participant receives an “I Showed Up” award , a playful take on participation awards that includes a fun swag bag or treat alongside a thoughtfully designed medal. Because showing up counts, and we fully embrace it. Each event features a playful theme that encourages dressing up, having fun, and leaning into the experience. Race morning includes our signature Bib Bedazzle Station so you can add personal flair and glam before hitting the course. Expect high-energy, bass-heavy music to keep the vibes up from start to finish. Our Lucky Duck Hunt adds a playful, interactive twist that rewards curiosity and participation. We wrap up each event with a post-race Raffle as our way of saying thanks for showing up and hanging out. Whether you run, jog, or walk, Hobby Joggers creates a no-pressure, stress-free environment where all paces and bodies are welcomed and celebrated. This is not your average race experience. We RUN FOR FUN.

Description:
Howl-O-Ween Dog Run 5K & 1 Miler Granada Beach – 5000 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803 Get ready for a paws-itively spooky good time at the Howl-O-Ween Dog Run — where runners and their four-legged besties hit the beach for a fun, festive morning full of costumes, community, and coastal vibes. Whether you’re chasing a PR or just out for a fun jog (or stroll) with your pup, this event is all about good energy, wagging tails, and unforgettable moments. Race Day Schedule: • 8:30 AM – 5K Start • 8:45 AM – 1 Miler Start What to Expect: • Flat, fast, paved beach path course • Dog-friendly stroller-friendly (bring your crew!) • Professional chip timing for the 5K • Free race day photos (no upsells, ever) • Overall & age group awards • Costume contest for runners and pups • Finish line festival with music good vibes Costumes Highly Encouraged! From spooky to silly to straight-up ridiculous — dress up with your dog and go all out. We’ll be awarding the best dressed humans and pups! The CaliFlow Vibe: This isn’t just a race — it’s a morning at the beach with your community. Music playing, dogs wagging, people cheering… and that energy you only get at a CaliFlow event. So leash up your pup, throw on a costume, and come run (or walk) with us. Come for the run. Stay for the vibe. ✨

Here's why you should participate : It's a great way to get active and have fun! Whether you're a seasoned runner or a casual walker, this event is for everyone. Description:
What will you find at the Huntington Lake triathlon? Finisher's Medal Event T-Shirt Pancake breakfast Rosa Brother's Chocolate Milk Prizes and Giveaways Complimentary Race Photos The Huntington Lake Triathlon is a fun and challenging race in an incredible location in Lakeshore, CA near the China Peak Resort. This event features a lake swim in Huntington Lake, a challenging road bike course, and a ‘high altitude’ run, which is part trail and part paved, finishes the race. Each athlete registered for the Huntington Lake Triathlon will receive a custom t-shirt, athlete goody bag, swim cap, post-race meal, and be eligible for raffle prizes and race awards three-deep in each division. Take the weekend and come up and enjoy this fun event with your family. Note: A USAT membership is required for the Triathlon, (but not the 5k/10k) If you do not have one, you can purchase one during the registration process. Parking : There is a $10 vehicle entrance fee. We recommend car pooling if possible. Volunteer : Earn a future discounted multisport or free run! Transferable and never expires.

Born from my personal journey with Stage IV mediastinal paraganglioma, JP’s Backyard Ultra is a fundraiser for the Pheo Para Alliance , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 26-1510652) dedicated to empowering patients, families, and medical professionals affected by pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma through education, advocacy, and global support. Scroll down for map below. Participants can choose anywhere from 1 to 10 loops. Runners and hikers alike start at the same time every hour going clockwise on the even hours and counterclockwise on the odd hours. So it doesn't matter if you finish your loop fast or slow because everyone starts again at the same time in the next hour. Description:
Join us for JP’s Backyard Ultra, a one-of-a-kind ultramarathon and hike set in the scenic trails of Skyline Wilderness Park in Napa, CA. Now in its fourth and final year, this grassroots event is more than just a race, it’s a celebration of life, resilience, and community. Born from my personal journey with Stage IV mediastinal paraganglioma, JP’s Backyard Ultra is a fundraiser for the Pheo Para Alliance , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 26-1510652) dedicated to empowering patients, families, and medical professionals affected by pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma through education, advocacy, and global support. Learn more at www.pheopara.org . Whether you're in it for one loop or ten, come run or hike in solidarity, to honor those facing rare diseases, to challenge yourself, and to stand as part of a growing force for good. ~Jonathan Pascual The course features a 3.3 mile loop with 550 feet of climbing, offering a mix of terrain from steep rocky sections to shaded paths. Scroll down for map below. Participants can choose anywhere from 1 to 10 loops. Runners and hikers alike start at the same time every hour going clockwise on the even hours and counterclockwise on the odd hours. So it doesn't matter if you finish your loop fast or slow because everyone starts again at the same time in the next hour. Those attempting 10 loops should pace themselves for a final race on the 10th loop making 33.3 miles. You can do as many or as few loops as you wish however. Timed Event: 8:00 AM - 6:

Race name: Juneteenth Freedom Run/Walk
Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
The Juneteenth Freedom 5K/5 Mile Run is an event that preserves history with significant meaning and direct community benefit. Juneteenth commemorates the day when 250,000 slaves in Texas were declared free. Our race began in 2021 when Juneteenth was designated a federal holiday and we are celebrating our 5th year! This year we are partnering with the Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc., Iota Nu Lambda Chapter for their excellence in generating scholarships for college-bound youth and launching 4 scholarships from race profits. The goods: All participants in the live and virtual races will receive a tech shirt and medal. The live 5K/5 Mile race will receive a bag with goodies and will be eligible for placement award trophies. We will offer cash prizes for breaking the course record for the 5K and 5 mile races. The 5 Mile race is a 20-point race in the Central Valley Runner of the Year series.

This exciting challenge allows you to raise funds and awareness for those battling cancer all while having fun! 100% of the funds will benefit the Kern County Cancer Foundation to assist local patients with medical bills related to cancer treatment as well as assist children with cancer who must travel for treatment. For more information on our programs and services visit us at www.kerncountycancerfoundation.org This is our 13th Annual KERN CANCER RUN/WALK and FESTIVAL EVENT and we couldn't do it without you ! It will be held Saturday, September 12th from 8am - 1pm at Riverwalk Park in Bakersfield, CA. Early registration is $10, then the cost goes up to $20 after March 31, 2026. Children registration is $10 ages 3-11. Kern County Cancer Run/Walk T-Shirts can be purchased for $20 with a deadline of 8/23/2026. Survivors are FREE and there will be a special designated area for them. (Even if you're on treatment, you're a SURVIVOR) This race will be timed for all registered runners and awards will be given. Top fundraising teams and individual will also receive awards. We are trying to raise as much funds as possible for Kern County cancer patients who need financial assistance and transportation during treatment. Some T-shirts will be available for sale at the event. Donations are always welcome. *PLEASE BE MINDFUL OF THOSE AROUND YOU, ESPECIAL

Race name: Kristina Chesterman Memorial Run
Listed distance: 10K
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Please join in supporting the Kristina Chesterman Memorial Clinic in Nigeria by participating in, or cheering on the 5-10k run. Kristina Chesterman was a vibrant and compassionate nursing student at California State University, Chico. Tragically, in September 2013, her life was cut short when she was struck by a drunk driver while riding her bike. Despite her untimely passing, Kristina's spirit of generosity continues to inspire many. As an organ donor, she saved the lives of five individuals, and one baby who received portions of her liver and a 64-year-old woman who received her heart. In her honor, the Kristina Chesterman Memorial Foundation was established to support nursing students and public health initiatives in underserved communities. One of its significant achievements is the Kristina Chesterman Memorial Clinic in rural Nigeria, which opened in 2019. This clinic provides essential medical care to a community in great need, fulfilling Kristina's dream of making a global impact through nursing.

Race name: Lace Up For Learning
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Lace Up For Learning is a nonprofit that was started in 2024 by five 8th grade friends who believe in the value of community, the importance of education, and the power of running. The mission behind this annual event is to raise money for under resourced classrooms across the greater Sacramento area. In the first two years, participants, donors, and sponsors raised more than $30,000 -- reaching thousands of students, K-12. The 5k and 10k courses run on the beautiful, flat paved Parkway Trails in Folsom. The Kids Fun Run includes obstacle elements and takes place on a large grass field. Participants of all levels are welcome - from serious runners to community supporters pushing strollers or walking their dogs. We look forward to meeting you on race day - and we appreciate your support for our mission.

Race name: Lafayette Res Run for Education
Listed distance: 5K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
About the Lafayette Res Run for Education The Lafayette Chamber and the City of Lafayette are co-sponsors of the Lafayette Res Run for Education which is traditionally held the third Sunday in October. The 2025 Lafayette Res Run for Education will be held Sunday, October 19. 5k: 8am, 10k: 8:15am, 2 mile: 8:45am in downtown Lafayette, CA. Back by popular demand, from its introduction in 2020, you can register for the Reservoir Challenge – the virtual race which “runs” around the 2.7-mile paved trail of the Lafayette Reservoir October 11-18. Please note, the Reservoir Challenge is not an option on Sunday, October 19 as the Reservoir will be closed for the 10K runners. The Reservoir Challenge is great opportunity to safely walk or run the Reservoir on your own, perhaps beating your time from last year. Beneficiaries of the event are the local schools and the services and programs of the Chamber. See below for what we gave back to our schools last year! The Run is the city’s most popular “family affair”, involving kids, parents, grandparents, and hundreds of serious runners from throughout the Bay Area. Join us in 2025 for the 10k, 5k, the 2 mile run/walk for fun or the Reservoir Challenge! Sprinters, walkers, the “stroller brigade” and many of Lafayette’s top four legged residents are welcome to join in the fun. The first 100 students to register from each school will receive a voucher for a free 1/4 pound of bulk candy from Zoonie's during packet pickup! Packet Pickup Race pack

Description:
Join us in Healdsburg, California, on April 11th 2026 for the TERREX Lake Sonoma 100K, 50K, and Trail Sisters Half Marathon! We are excited to have adidas TERREX back as our presenting partner! We are stoked to team up with Mountain Outpost to bring you full livestream coverage, athlete panels, interviews, and commentary from special guests! Lake Sonoma 100K The 100K course will start with a climb up Pritchett Peak with a water only stop at the top. Over the years, participation has grown significantly, expanding to welcome members of the public. Today, more than 300 runners join us, and the Mug Run continues to foster friendly competition and positive engagement between law enforcement and the community. Each year, LASAA partners with Sheriff’s stations across the county to host a series of Mug Runs. Each station brings its own spirit, culture, and traditions to the event. This year, Altadena Station is dedicating their Mug Run to commemorating the two-year anniversary of the Altadena Eaton Fire. One year after the fire blackened the ridges above our town, the inaugural Altadena Forever Run stands as a symbol of resilience and recovery. It honors those who were affected, those who responded, and those who continue working to rebuild and strengthen our community. The Altadena Forever Run welcomes everyone. Event proceeds are donated to the following youth organizations: Boys & Girls Clubs of Silicon Valley Santa Clara County Office of Education YMCA of Silicon Valley

Description:
On Mean Girls Day, October 3rd, 2026 he asked you what day it was. You said it’s October 3rd. Now lace up and run. Welcome to The Mean Girls 5K, 10K and Half Marathon, a pink powered comedy fueled tribute to the most quotable high school ever. This event transforms the LA River Path into North Shore High where every runner is either trying to make fetch happen or survive gym class without being personally victimized by Regina George. Presented by Jed and Ted’s Excellent Races. Wear pink if it’s Wednesday. Wear sweatpants only if it’s Saturday. Do not wear army pants and flip flops unless you want everyone else to buy army pants and flip flops. This is your chance to run like you’re late for Calc, dodge Regina’s bus, and earn a medal pretty enough for the Spring Fling Court. Choose your challenge: The Burn Book 5K - A fast and funny out and back perfect for anyone who wants to run, walk, gossip, or talk about how butter is a carb. The Glen Coco 10K - Six point two miles of pure candy cane energy. You go Glen Coco. Treat yourself and your friends. None for Gretchen Wieners. The Full Plastics Half Marathon - Thirteen point one miles of pure drama control. Stay hydrated. Stay cute. Try not to start a three way call attack. Cross the finish feeling like the new Spring Fling Queen. The Multiverse Lunch Table Dash (Virtual) - Run from anywhere. Work. School. Your bedroom. Africa. Description:
The Menlo Park Kids Triathlon (“MPKT”) is a triathlon specifically for kids ages from 4 to 17 years old. A triathlon is a race that consists of a combination of three sports: swimming, cycling, and running. The kids start the race with swimming at the Burgess Pool in waves (triathlon speak for groups) of 20 to 25 kids. From the swim, they run to the transition area to put on their helmets, shoes, and anything else they need. They then mount their bikes and head out to the bike course. When the kids are done with the bike, they head back to transition to put their bike away, and head to run round Burgess Park. They finish the race in the park by crossing through the finishing chute!

A triathlon is a race that consists of a combination of three sports: swimming, cycling, and running. The kids start the race with swimming at the Burgess Pool in waves (triathlon speak for groups) of 20 to 25 kids. From the swim, they run to the transition area to put on their helmets, shoes, and anything else they need. They then mount their bikes and head out to the bike course. When the kids are done with the bike, they head back to transition to put their bike away, and head to run round Burgess Park. They finish the race in the park by crossing through the finishing chute!

Race name: Merced River Canyon Run - Burma Grade and McCabe Flat
Listed distance: 5 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Mariposa county's classic Merced River Canyon Race returns this year with two options for runners. McCabe Flat Flat out. T his 5 mile race is from the Briceburg bridge to McCabe Flat campground and back (2.5 each way). As the name suggests this race is about as flat as a race in the foothills can be. This race can be done at any pace but some will choose to try and set a record on the flattest footrace in the county. Burma Grade . This 9 mile race starts at the river level and climbs up the mighty Burma Grade (4.5 each way). This race offers the most elevation of any foot race in the county and leaves the racers with an amazing sense of accomplishment. Both races are on hardpacked unpaved roads and offer amazing scenery in the Merced River Canyon. Note on location and directions, please take highway 140 to get to Briceburg. While there are other ways to get here, they are not recommend, especially not on race day.

Finisher's Medal Prizes and Giveaways Free Race Photos Get an Event T-Shirt included in the price of the triathlon The Millerton Lake Sprint Triathlon has long been known as a great first lake swim triathlon, and a warm up for the upcoming season. But don't let the bike and run distances fool you, there are a few steep hills on the ride, and the trail portion of run is a challenge. More of a good thing... The Olympic Distance has a more challenging swim, two loops of the bike course, and two loops of the run course with a trail run heading out, a paved road coming back and beautiful Millerton Lake as the backdrop. Note: A USAT membership is required for the Triathlon, (but not the 5k/10k) If you do not have one, you can purchase one during the registration process. Per USAT rules, multisport participants must present ID and USAT membership card at packet pickup. Total participation at this event is capped at 200. Register before it is sold out. There is a $10 vehicle entrance fee.

Race name: Millerton Madness Triathlon
Listed distance: 10.8 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
USAT Sanctioned Super Sprint Triathlon. Perfect for beginners, or a tune-up before your next big race. 400 yd swim | 5.4 mile bike | 2.2 mile run Swim: Starting in the water at Millerton, athletes will utilize Millerton Lake Boat Launch. Athletes will swim 400 yards around buoys, back to the boat ramp, exit the water and proceed to the Transition Area. Bike: Starting at the Transition Area, athletes will make their way north towards the Millerton park entrance, to the turnaround at the top Millerton Lake SRA sign. The bike is out and back with rolling hills. Returning to the transition area. Run: Run is all asphalt road. Starting at the Transition Area, athletes head north from the parking lot along the street for approximately 1.1 miles towards the Millerton park entrance to the turn around, (at the crosswalk), and back to the finish line.

Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Mindful Miles 5K Run/Walk aims to support mental health awareness. With support from a grant provided by the California Mental Health Services Authority (CalMHSA), we aim to promote understanding of mental health, how to support a healthy mind, and to promote the importance of physical activity, social engagement, and connections with community resources that support positive mental health. Start and Finish will be on the Yuba College track with an 8:30am warm-up and announcements and a 9:00am start. Breakfast will be served at 7:30am and awards at 10:00am. Same day registrations are open and available on the day of the run; however, T-Shirts are not guaranteed if registrations are on race day. Early Packet Pickup will be available at the Yuba County Office of Education Prevention Support and Services, 1010 I street, Marysville, California, 95901. If you are unable to make it, you may pick up your race packet in the morning from 7:30am - 8:30am at the Yuba College Track Field.

Race name: Morgan Hill Freedom Run
Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
The Freedom Run is a premiere event at Morgan Hill’s annual Freedom Fest, one of the few all-day Independence Day celebrations in the Bay Area. Start your 4th of July celebration with a morning race that will take you through Morgan Hill’s historic, tree-lined downtown. Then stay for the award-winning parade, the largest privately organized parade in Northern California and the official 4th of July Parade of Santa Clara County. The Freedom Fest’s annual events also include the Patriotic Sing, Family Street Dance, Freedom Car Cruise and Show, and the spectacular fireworks and entertainment show, Fireworks on the Green. Celebrated in our historic downtown core, the Community and Cultural Center as well as the Outdoor Sports Center, our six events deliver a spectacular, fun-filled, family-friendly celebration every July 4th holiday! Bib pickup will be Saturday June 27, 2026 from 10am to 2pm in the parking lot of the LDS church at 1790 E. Dunne Ave in Morgan Hill. There will be a second bib pickup day on July 2 or July 3 with time TBA. Bibs can also be picked up the morning of the race from 6:45am-7:30am at 17575 Peak Ave, near the finish line. Visit the race website for more information.

Race name: Mount Wilson Trail Race 2026
Listed distance: 8.6 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
The Mount Wilson Trail Race returns this year and will be held on Saturday, May 23rd, 2026. Race start time is 7:30 a.m., with packet pickup beginning at 6:00 a.m. that day. This will be the full 8.6 mile course from Kersting Court, up the Mount Wilson Trail to Orchard Camp, and back. Join us in donating to the Fletcher Trail Maintenance Fund, which supports our dedicated Trail Maintenance Crew volunteers with the necessary equipment, materials, supplies and tools. Your donation is greatly appreciated and makes a real difference for this historic trail running event and community! Our History : First run in 1908, the annual Mount Wilson Trail Race is one of the oldest trail races in California. The elevation gain is over 2,160 feet on a winding course. The original path, first used by the Gabrielino Indians, was dug out by Benjamin Don Benito Wilson in 1864.

Race name: Mountains 2 Beach Marathon and Half
Listed distance: 26.2 Miles
Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Uniquely situated and completely surrounded by beautiful mountains, the city of Ojai holds the start of the Mountains 2 Beach Marathon while the half starts closer to the beach. This point to point race winds through the Ventura River Valley as it makes its way to the pristine beaches of the last great surf town in California, Ventura. Runners will love the gradual downhill nature of the race, which is prime to make you faster but not hurt the knees, and the amazing weather of the area. After a final tour of beach front Ventura, runners and their families are treated to a finish line party only steps away from the surf and the shops and restaurants of Historic Downtown Ventura. As a certified Boston Qualifier, the courses, the race and the surrounding communities make for the perfect destination marathon and half.

Description:
Native American Health Center (NAHC) is excited to announce our 25th Running Is My High (RIMH) 5k/10k Fun Run and Walk themed 25 Years in Motion on Saturday, June 6th, 2026 at the Fairy Land area of Lake Merritt; 699 Bellevue Ave., Oakland, CA 94610. NAHC created Running is My High to engage community from all walks of life in an event promoting physical, mental, and cultural health. This special event will feature programming that honors Community Health and Native American cultural practices; includes guest speakers; and features outreach tables to connect our community to helpful resources. Online registration closes on June 5th and costs $30 for adults and $15 for youth, in-person registration on the day of the event (6/6) is $35 for adults and $20 for youth. We will see you at the starting line!

Race name: Napa Half Marathon
Listed distance: 13.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
The Napa Half Marathon is nestled up in the rolling hills of east Napa. Scenic, rustic and winding roads will take you from the start at Skyline Park through the vineyard lined neighborhoods in a charming countryside setting. Locals come out to cheer you on while curious deer are commonly seen along the course! Finishers of the Half Marathon will be greeted with a bottle of Napa Valley wine and all race finishers will receive a custom medal. The race is hosted by Athletic Feat and is professionally chip timed by SVE Timing. The Half Marathon starts at 7:30am. (Participants must be at least 12 years old on race day.) A fun distance for those who enjoy shorter races! The quarter marathon (about 6.55 miles) will follow the half marathon route on the first of its two loops. Then it will return to Skyline Park. Finishers will receive a medal and a bottle of wine. The quarter marathon will start with the Half, at 7:30am.

Race name: Nixon 5K for Title IX
Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
Celebrate the women and girls in your life in this family-friendly event to commemorate the achievements of Title IX, the landmark equality legislation signed by President Nixon fifty-three years ago. Bring your family, friends, sports teams and community groups to the NIXON 5K FOR TITLE IX and run (or walk) this moderate course following Yorba Linda’s El Cajon Trail. Athletes are encouraged to wear their favorite team gear supporting female sports! This is accessible for runners of all levels; strollers are welcome and dogs are allowed. Following the race, guests are invited to stop by the vendor fair in the Library parking lot!

Listed distance: 15K
Listed difficulty: Easy

Description:
Explore San Carlos' outstanding trail system as a runner in the fourth annual No Foolin' Foot Race! There's something for everyone with four challenging events through Big Canyon, Eaton and Pulgas Ridge . 1K (~350ft of climbing) - Perfect for adventurous kids age 5-10 5k (~530ft of climbing) 10k (~1,500ft of climbing) Long Course NEW this year! (15K with ~2,300ft of climbing) Early bird pricing available through March 18, 2026. Consider yourself warned: This race is no joke! Our courses are technical, grueling and loads of fun. We will be hosting course previews on Sunday, March 8 (5K and 10K routes) and Saturday, March 28 (5K and 15K routes) in partnership with A Runner's Mind and Brooks. RSVP on Strava , and j oin our Strava Club for updates. Start and Finish Festival at Crestview Park. Professional timing; Tech-Ts and free runner photos for all participants; Awards in multiple categories. All proceeds benefit maintenance and improvement of San Carlos open space trails. A race is only as good as its crew! We have many exciting volunteer opportunities. All volunteers receive a free t-shirt and complimentary entry in next year's race. Sign up here . Presented by Kaiser Permanente in partnership with the Parks and Recreation Foundation of San Carlos and the City of San Carlos.

Description:
Join us on Saturday, August 8, 2026 for the 10th annual Noyo Headlands Race. This year we'll have a half marathon, 10K run, 5k run, 5k fun walk, and half-mile kids' run along the stunning coastal trail in Fort Bragg, CA. Enjoy some of the most remarkable scenery Northern California has to offer and have a great time running with your friends! The oceanfront trail consists of asphalt and soft track, is fairly flat, well maintained, and commonly used by runners year-round. This race benefits Mendocino Land Trust in its mission to conserve and restore habitat, scenic areas and working lands while also providing public access to beautiful places in and around Mendocino County.

Will you run and be their heroes by joining the Nurses Rock Run-Walk 5K-10k & BONNIE CHALLENGE? We have all learned how incredibly valuable our nurses are to our health care system. In 2026 we will be offering the live experience and a virtual run to provide the perfect opportunity and flexibility to participate safely while interacting with our nursing and running community live & online to support a great cause. Sign up TODAY and join us as we culminate your work on running and our audience of future nurses. Whether you run or walk, by yourself or with friends, you will make a HUGE IMPACT for our nurses and the future of the nursing profession! As we continue with our planning, your support or donation of any kind is always appreciated in that it will go towards helping more amazing nursing students while bringing awareness to the nursing shortage that impacts each and every one of us. They are our heroes and you are theirs. Register NOW and let's get moving! *START GETTING YOUR GROUPS TOGETHER! AWARDS FOR OUR TOP 3 LARGEST GROUPS! Directions to Frank G. OneLegacy Donate Life Run Walk is back! Join us for our 2026 OneLegacy Donate Life Run Walk to run or walk with your team and celebrate the power of organ, eye and tissue donation. The event features an inspiring opening ceremony, competitive 5K run and healthy 5K/1K walk, followed by a Family Festival with food vendors, live entertainment, special activities for children and a raffle drawing. A non-competitive 5K/1K Run/Walk to educate and inspire the community about organ, eye, and tissue donation with proceeds benefiting the OneLegacy Foundation. LOCATION: Azusa Pacific University, 701 E Foothill Blvd, Azusa, California 91702 DATE: April 25, 2026 EVENT SCHEDULE: 7:00 am Registration 8:30 am Opening Ceremony 9:20 am 5K Run/Walk starts 9:40 am 1K Run/Walk starts 7:00 am to 12:00 pm Family Festival with food, opportunity prizes, children's activities, vendors and more! Please practice social distancing as best you can; we want everyone to be safe and healthy.

Description:
The Pacific Coast Triathlon invites athletes of all ages and abilities — from first-timers to seasoned competitors — to experience one of Southern California’s most scenic and celebrated races at the stunning Crystal Cove State Beach. Start your day with a refreshing open-water swim in the Pacific Ocean right at Crystal Cove State Beach. Full lifeguard support and typically comfortable wave conditions make this leg welcoming for every level. Choose the Sprint (½ mile / ~750 m) or Olympic (1,500 m). Next, tackle the bike on a fully closed, rolling course along the iconic Pacific Coast Highway. Enjoy sweeping ocean views as you ride two loops for the Sprint (12 miles) or four loops for the Olympic (40K / ~24.8 miles). The run winds along the gorgeous Crystal Cove Trail and paths, with panoramic ocean views on one side and Pacific Coast Highway on the other. You’ll pass through the historic beach cottages, and — when tides allow — enjoy a memorable stretch right along the sand before climbing back up for an unforgettable oceanfront finish. Sprint runners cover 3 miles; Olympic athletes run 6.2 miles (10K), with aid stations every mile. Additional race options include Sprint & Olympic Duathlon, Aquabike, Relay teams (male, female, or co-ed), and a 5K Beach and Trail Run. This USAT-sanctioned event is part of the popular OC Tri Series and proudly supports local non-profits. Every finisher receives a custom medal (plus official race shirt and other great swag). Next, tackle the bike on a fully closed, rolling course along the iconic Pacific Coast Highway. The run winds along the gorgeous Crystal Cove Trail and paths, with panoramic ocean views on one side and Pacific Coast Highway on the other. You’ll pass through the historic beach cottages, and — when tides allow — enjoy a memorable stretch right along the sand before climbing back up for an unforgettable oceanfront finish. Sprint runners cover 3 miles; Olympic athletes run 6.2 miles (10K), with aid stations every mile. Additional race options include Sprint & Olympic Duathlon, Aquabike, Relay teams (male, female, or co-ed), and a 5K Beach and Trail Run. This USAT-sanctioned event is part of the popular OC Tri Series and proudly supports local non-profits. Every finisher receives a custom medal (plus official race shirt and other great swag). What You Get (Swag Bag) : - Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only) - Finisher's Towel or Giveaway - Finisher's Medal! - Digital Training Pack - Online Results & Certif

Listed distance: 3.1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
The Daffodil race has been a staple for the Nevada County community for many, many years. Offering a 5K and a 10K, the routes travel through the quaint little town of Penn Valley and across the green rolling hills on country roads. The 5K travels along the edge of Western Gateway Park, past the dog park, and finally to the park and ride for a quick turnaround for a return to the finish. The 10K begins the same as the 5K, but will take a detour through the park before heading to the park and ride. During the return, the 10K turns right and weaves through the rural countryside of Penn Valley before racing back to the finish. The Penn Valley Chamber will be serving a pancake breakfast for a small cost and the Penn Valley Lions will be the course marshals on the road. Listed difficulty: Moderate

Description:
Swim 1.5 miles from Scripps Pier to La Jolla Cove. This is an organized and timed event with awards to the top finishers. At the finish, you will be greeted by LJCSC volunteers, breakfast provided by Duke's of La Jolla, awards for regulation top finishers, awards for regulation age group winners, and participant swag. EVENT INFORMATION Registration 7:30-8:30 AM at La Jolla Shores NOTE: Registration Location: La Jolla Shores Beach, Kellogg Park, North End (North side of parking lot; near north end bathrooms; setup on grass). Swimmers will walk from there to the Pier, about ¼ mile away. The swim will start on the north side of Scripps Pier at 9:00 AM. Swimmer safety is our first priority. San Diego Lifeguards will watch over swimmers from a boat, jet skis, and paddleboards. Beach REGISTRATION and PRE-REGISTERED CHECK-IN is 7:30 - 8:30 AM NOTE: REGISTRATION LOCATION: LA JOLLA SHORES KELLOGG PARK NORTH END (North end of main parking lot) There is a large free parking lot at the registration area and parking is plentiful, especially if you arrive early. You can also carpool, UBER, LYFT, or have someone drop you off. If you need a ride from La Jolla Cove to Registration , we will offer limited, free shuttle service from the Cove starting at 7:15 AM until around 8:15 AM. Shuttle service is not guaranteed, especially if you arrive late.

Listed distance: 1 Miles
Listed difficulty: Beginner

Description:
1 mile. Straight up. This will be a chip timed hill climb starting at the San Joaquin River Trailhead in the South Finegold picnic area (Millerton Lk SRA; end of Sky Harbor Rd) and finishing at the top of Pincushion Mountain. There will be a special prize for the Top 3 Male and Female finishers, age groups winners will receive awards as well as Clydesdale/Athena division winners. All runners will receive a custom finisher award and event shirt. Pincushion Hill Climb: Mountain Goat Edition! The Mountain Goat race is for those who like to go the extra mile or miles. Your first run up will be timed and scored for the regular event then you have until 12pm (4hrs total) to complete as many trips up to Pincushion Peak as possible. Your first trip down you must take the long way (just over 1.5 miles) after that you may descend the same route you take to the top. You must complete at least 2 trips to the top in order to be considered a Mountain Goat. You will receive a special finishers award and the top Male & Female runners will receive an additional award.

No parking will be allowed at Pleasanton Middle School or Hearst Elementary school 2 Mile, 5K, 10K & ENTRY INCLUDES Race entry includes a short sleeve performance blend t-shirt (cotton/polyester blend), race timing (5K/10K), commemorative bib number, eligibility for age group and overall awards (5K/10K), finisher medal, and post-race refreshments. All ages are welcome to participate in these three divisions; there is no minimum age. Option to upgrade to a technical race t-shirt (tri-blend poly/cotton/rayon jersey) available in men's sizing for $10.00. One may opt-out of the t-shirt

This is winter running at its best. ❄️ What’s Included ✔ Professional Chip Timing for accurate results Free Race Photos – download and share your frosty finish ️ Finisher Medal for All Participants Overall & Age Group Awards Three On-Course Water Stations Finish Line Party with music and high vibes Who Can Participate?
